title: bug: Restart Daemon kills whatever pid a repository-supplied .moe/daemon.json names
description: MoeProjectService.restartDaemon reads .moe/daemon.json and calls ProcessHandle.of(info.pid).destroy() whenever that pid is alive, with no provenance check. readDaemonInfo also skips its project-path check when projectPath is empty. A repository can commit .moe/daemon.json naming any pid the user may signal, and the Restart Daemon button then kills that process. Under the protected profile, gate the kill on RuntimeSelectionPolicy.verifyProvenance, or kill only the supervisor's own spawned process. Found by CQ-R01 (task-3b760109c42544ab892199b3d5534b77), whose plan scopes MoeProjectService to the doConnect/connect gates.
definitionOfDone: Under the protected profile, Restart Daemon never signals a process whose provenance RuntimeSelectionPolicy.verifyProvenance does not confirm
Legacy Restart Daemon behavior is unchanged, or the change is explicitly decided and tested

implementationPlan.description: Add restart regressions to RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest using its existing service/project/status fixtures and a proposed injected supervisor ProcessHandle resolver returning inert spy handles. Cover PROTECTED unrecorded PID, stale start/PID reuse, another project's record, empty daemon.json projectPath, missing start information and malformed-profile fail-closed selection: zero destroy calls. Cover a recorded supervisor/direct child allowed exactly once, dead/absent process allowing stale metadata cleanup, and LEGACY unrecorded live PID preserving its prior signal/cleanup/reconnect semantics. Exercise real service.restartDaemon on refusal: metadata bytes preserved, refusal status visible, no new process start or retry/backoff reset. Test resolver/signal exceptions and destroy=false under protected vs legacy; never call destroy on the test JVM or any external process.

Move only the restart PID-signal operation into a small supervisor method (proposed stopDaemonForRestart(info): String?, null = may continue, string = refusal). Add an optional trailing ProcessHandle lookup constructor dependency defaulting to ProcessHandle.of(pid).orElse(null), consistent with current probes. Preserve the existing live/dead decision; capture a live target handle once, require activationRefusal(info)==null under the protected profile immediately before signaling, then destroy that captured handle rather than resolving the PID again. Missing/dead handle is no signal. Under PROTECTED a provenance refusal or lookup/signal error/false destroy fails closed with a bounded actionable reason; error handling must not fall through to cleanup or reconnect. LEGACY keeps the old best-effort signal behavior, including continuing after signal failure. Do not use argv, repo metadata ownership claims, killSpawnedDaemon fallback or a new trust mechanism. Keep a short why-comment explaining repository metadata is not authority.

Route restartDaemon through that supervisor stop method and remove its direct ProcessHandle.destroy path. After existing disconnect, if a stop refusal is returned, publishStatus(false, reason) and return before deleting daemon.json, resetting spawn/reconnect state or calling connect. Otherwise retain current stale-file deletion/backoff/reconnect flow. Missing or malformed metadata must never supply a signal target; preserve readDaemonInfo compatibility rather than changing global discovery rules. Keep UI guidance clear that an unverified process must be independently identified/stopped; no claim that a PID read from the repo is the daemon. Extend the tests from step 1 to pin the real service wiring and allowed branch; no test-only alternate restart implementation.

Single verification gate: acquire jetbrains-gradle lease and from repository root run exactly `(cd moe-jetbrains && MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 cmd.exe /d /c "set GRADLE_OPTS=-Xmx512m&& gradlew.bat test --rerun")`; release lease even on failure. This is the native-Windows equivalent of the task's ./gradlew test on this WSL host without Java. Require :test actually executes, fresh XML contains the new protected/legacy restart tests, and zero test failures/errors. Supply fresh command/exitCode/outputTail to complete_task. No daemon/proxy regression for this Kotlin-only mid-epic task. Tests use fake signal targets and temporary metadata on all platforms, not OS kill commands.

Final adversarial self-review once with adversarial-self-review: trace every restart signal and refusal path; verify forged metadata including blank projectPath cannot authorize protected kill, PID/start/project identity is checked by existing policy, captured handle is not replaced after authorization, and failed signals cannot continue protected cleanup. Check repeated/concurrent restart, dead-process disappearance, malformed settings, null/missing metadata and exact legacy behavior. Inspect both service and supervisor tests against production wiring, not an unused helper. This does not certify OS-atomic restart/port binding or enable verified-local; those CQ-R13 concerns remain. If review changes code, rerun the same gate before complete_task.

comments.content: From CQ-R01 (task-3b760109c42544ab892199b3d5534b77) step-8 review: under the protected profile the activation refusal tells the user "Stop it, then use Restart Daemon." (RuntimeSelectionPolicy.verifyProvenance refusal text). Once the user has stopped that daemon, the pid in the repository-supplied .moe/daemon.json is dead or reused, so following the advice is exactly the path where restartDaemon kills an unrelated process. Fixing this bug should make restartDaemon verify the pid (e.g. RuntimeSelectionPolicy.verifyProvenance / a recorded spawn under PROTECTED, start instant + command under legacy) before destroying it; the refusal text can stay as is.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Reuse the landed RuntimeSelectionPolicy provenance via MoeDaemonSupervisor.activationRefusal; do not add another trust registry or infer ownership from daemon.json/argv. Preserve LEGACY behavior as the task permits; protect PROTECTED restart and surface refusal. Encapsulate only the existing PID-signal operation in the supervisor so tests can safely inject a ProcessHandle resolver. Three files, no schema/wire changes; CQ-R13 retains broader recovery/provenance work.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: restartDaemon currently disconnects, reads repo metadata, checks isProcessAlive, destroys ProcessHandle.of(pid), deletes metadata, resets backoff and connects. activationRefusal already calls verifyProvenance only under PROTECTED; its per-project pid/start records reject reused/unowned processes. RuntimeSelectionPolicyTest has real service/fake Project/status fixtures and supervisor injection, plus current-process provenance tests. Existing supplier constructor seam patterns in MoeDaemonSupervisor make safe spy handles possible without ever killing a real process.
planningNotes.risks: Security boundary: refusal must return BEFORE metadata removal, reset/reconnect or any signal fallback. Capture target handle once before provenance check and destroy that handle, never resolve a new pid afterward. Liveness is not provenance. No source/config mutation or arbitrary PID termination in tests. Empty projectPath must not bypass provenance. No unsupported auto-replacement or stronger isolation claim. Preserve legacy swallowed-signal-error behavior deliberately. Windows processes use parent/supervisor provenance, not unavailable argv.
